title: Day 104: World Cup T-5 Days; Korea Day in Zapopan (CJNG Heartland); CJNG Blackout in Effect; El Sapo at Large Day 104
detail: Day 104 since El Mencho's killing at Tapalpa, Jalisco (February 22, 2026). KOREA DAY IN ZAPOPAN — CJNG HEARTLAND (June 6, 2026): South Korea's World Cup squad, based in Guadalajara for FIFA World Cup 2026, held 'Korea Day' (Día de Corea) on June 6 in Zapopan — the Guadalajara metro municipality that serves as CJNG's historic operational center. The public cultural event — featuring K-food, K-pop, and sports programming — drew international attention to Guadalajara's dual identity as both a World Cup host city and Mexico's foremost CJNG nexus. Seoul Economic Daily coverage noted the security shadow: InSight Crime analysts assessed organized crime groups are unlikely to target World Cup tourist events because cartels profit from tourism, but Jalisco state has logged approximately 16,000 disappearances — one of the highest totals in Mexico — and organized crime violence remains elevated throughout the metro area. The Korea Day event underscores the paradox of hosting international sporting events in a city where CJNG's structural presence remains intact despite 104 days of post-Mencho decapitation operations. Guadalajara hosts four FIFA World Cup group-stage matches beginning June 15. PLAN KUKULKAN — T-5 DAYS: Five days remain before the FIFA World Cup 2026 opening match (June 11, Estadio Azteca, Mexico City vs. South Africa). Mexico's security deployment remains at peak operational readiness: 99,000+ security personnel, 20,000 Armed Forces, 55,000 federal and state police, 188 canine units, 2,100 military vehicles, 24 aircraft and drone systems, anti-drone electronic warfare systems fully operational at all three Mexican venues. CJNG BLACKOUT DIRECTIVE — CONFIRMED ONGOING (Day 104): CJNG's internal operational directive to avoid high-visibility violence during the World Cup window continues in effect. Intelligence analysts assess this as temporary operational calculus; cartel violence expected to return to post-Mencho baseline after the tournament window closes. CJNG JUNE ATTACK TEMPO — HIGHEST OF POST-MENCHO PERIOD: Despite the high-visibility blackout, CJNG's June 2026 total attack count remains the highest monthly figure of the entire post-Mencho period — 324 total attacks in June (756 total attacks Feb–June 2026), reflecting ongoing low-profile territorial consolidation operations by El 03's Grupo Élite and Colombian mercenary-assisted offensives in Michoacán. EL SAPO HUNT — DAY 104: Hugo Gonzalo Mendoza Gaytán ('El Sapo' / 'El 090') remains at large as Mexico's #1 CJNG enforcement target on Day 104. Security posture has effectively pivoted from the pre-June 11 capture objective to World Cup perimeter protection. MANZANILLO COMMAND VOID — DAY 28: 28 days since El Chucky's May 9 arrest; no confirmed successor plaza boss at Mexico's primary fentanyl precursor port. CJNG COLOMBIAN MERCENARIES — PURÉPECHA PLATEAU (Ongoing): 60+ Colombian paramilitary operatives continue operating across 10 Michoacán municipalities. SUCCESSION BINARY (Day 104): El 03 (confirmed leader, financial wing, Grupo Élite) vs. El Sapo (military wing, at large). CIAGATE FGR INVESTIGATION: Ongoing. JUNE BILATERAL MULLIN MEETING: Not yet formally calendared.

media.caption: Korea Day in Zapopan, Guadalajara — South Korea's World Cup squad hosts cultural event in CJNG's historic operational heartland, T-5 days before the FIFA World Cup opening; Jalisco cartel shadow documented
